chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Sa'd ibn Abi Khalaf who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the unmarried man performing Hajj on behalf of the deceased. He said: Yes, if the unmarried man does not have enough to perform Hajj for himself, then if he has enough to perform Hajj for himself, it is not valid for the deceased until he performs Hajj from his own wealth. And it is valid for the deceased if the unmarried man has wealth, and if he does not have wealth.

key_terms.الصَّرُورَةُ: An unmarried man who has not yet married
key_terms.يَجُوزُ: Valid / Acceptable (in the context of ritual performance)
key_terms.يَحُجُّ عَنِ الْمَيِّتِ: Performing Hajj on behalf of the deceased

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an unmarried man performing Hajj on behalf of a deceased person if he has or lacks funds for his own Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar clarifies the priority of obligatory Hajj (Hajj al-Din) for the living over performing Hajj on behalf of the deceased. It establishes that an unmarried man (al-sarrur) who has not yet fulfilled his own obligatory Hajj cannot validly perform Hajj for a deceased person until he has either performed it himself or used his wealth to do so, ensuring the debt to God is cleared first. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that personal religious obligations take precedence over vicarious ones.
